dashboard.label: KML Overlay
dashboard.description: Demonstrates KML and KMZ overlay support with toggleable layer control entries.

html.p: Maps+ can load KML and KMZ files as overlay layers on top of your map. Each file is registered as a named, toggleable entry in the layer control widget.
Local files are served from appserver/static/visualizations/maps-plus/contrib/kml/ inside the app. Specify just the filename (e.g. sample.kml).
Remote files are fetched by URL. Use the full https:// address.
Multiple files can be loaded at once by separating them with commas in the KML Overlay formatter option. Each file gets its own toggle in the layer control.
Loads contrib/kml/sample.kml — a bundled file with three US region polygons (Northwest, Northeast, South).
The layer control entry is labeled sample.kml. Toggling it hides or shows all polygons. Clicking a polygon shows a popup with its name.
Use this pattern for KML files you ship inside the app package.
Loads contrib/kml/sample.kmz — the same three US region polygons as the KML panel, packaged as a KMZ (zipped KML).
Maps+ uses JSZip to extract the KML from the archive automatically. The layer control entry is labeled sample.kmz.
KMZ support means you can ship compressed overlays without any extra configuration.

panel.title: Remote KML URL — NASA WorldWind Samples

html.p: Loads a KML file directly from an external URL. The full https:// address is passed to the KML Overlay option — no local copy needed.
This example uses NASA WorldWind KML Samples: colored polygons and placemarks near NASA Ames Research Center in Mountain View, CA.
The Splunk server must be able to reach the remote URL. Use this pattern for externally-hosted overlays, such as Splunk Cloud deployments.

panel.title: Multiple Overlays — local KML + remote KML + local KMZ

html.p: Comma-separate multiple filenames and URLs in the KML Overlay option to load them all at once. Each file gets its own named entry in the layer control — they can be toggled independently.
This panel loads three files simultaneously: a local KML, a remote KML URL, and a local KMZ. All three file types are supported in the same field.
